role_in_parent: Handles the previously missing size-1 subproblems and supplies the explicit value E_1=1.
statement_nl: Let t be the empty sign sequence, namely the unique sequence of length 0. Let F(t) be the number of permutations b=(b_1) of {1} such that all required sign inequalities hold vacuously. Then F(t)=1. In particular, if Alt_1^+ denotes the empty sign sequence and E_1 = F(Alt_1^+), then E_1=1.

domain_restrictions: t is exactly the unique sign sequence of length 0
b must be a permutation of the set containing only 1
the sign inequalities are vacuous because there are no sign positions to check
Alt_1^+ denotes the empty sign sequence
E_1 is defined only after identifying Alt_1^+ with the empty sign sequence
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: The empty sign sequence has exactly one compatible permutation of the singleton set containing 1, so F of the empty sign sequence equals 1. Since Alt_1^+ names the empty sign sequence and E_1 is defined as F of Alt_1^+, it follows that E_1 equals 1.
quantifier_order: Fix t as the unique empty sign sequence.
Consider permutations b of the singleton set containing 1.
Count those b for which the sign inequalities are all vacuous.
Define E_1 to be F of Alt_1^+, where Alt_1^+ is the empty sign sequence.

variables.name: F
variables.type: function from sign sequences to integers

variables.domain: permutations of the singleton set containing 1
variables.name: b
E_1
variables.role: value defined as F applied to Alt_1^+

witness_dependencies: No existential witness is needed; the count is over all permutations b of a singleton set
The fact that F(t) equals 1 depends on there being exactly one permutation of the singleton set containing 1
The conclusion E_1 equals 1 depends on the identification of Alt_1^+ with the empty sign sequence and on the definition E_1 = F(Alt_1^+)
